text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
CAPITAL
- The outgoing government of the Party of Social Democracy has left behind budgetary chaos, the paper says.
- East European Imports of the U.S. wants to import four-wheel drive vehicles made in Romania.
- The central bank is supporting the new OTC market, the paper says.
ADEVARUL
- Executives of IAR helicopter maker in Brasov to sign this week a cooperation deal with U.S. Bell Helicopters Textron to build 96 Cobra attack helicopters in Romania.
- Inflation, arrears and high interest rates have brought furniture makers to the brink of bankruptcy, the paper says.
- Chase Manhattan bank has allegedly delayed a $200 million revolving credit for Romania's crude oil imports.
- Prices of medicines expected to rise 60 percent by end-1996.
CRONICA ROMANA
- So far, the State Ownership Fund privatised 39.7 pct of the companies slated for privatisation.
- The Romanian Post-Privatisation Fund has become operational, the paper says.
- Pactinvest inaugurates new generation of mutual funds in Romania.
- Local companies have started to show interest in the stock exchange, the paper says.
JURNALUL NATIONAL
- The Romanian National Oil Company (CRP) id to continue activity, despite a court ruling to suspend it.
General:
All the newspapers report former tennis star Ilie Nastase's resignation from the outgoing Party of Social Democracy (PDSR)
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Opposition candidate Emil Constantinescu leads with 52.8 percent of vote intentions, while incumbent President Ion Iliescu would get 47.2 percent, according to a CURS polster.
- CURS poll shows some 24 percent of people polled have not made up their minds.
ADEVARUL

- "The President cannot control his advisers," reads a front-page headline presenting pictures of presidential adviser Dan Iosif making obscene gestures in front of the private PRO Tv television during the face-to-face debate of the two presidential contenders ahead of Sunday's run-off.

- The upper house, the Senate, debated two versions of a report drawn by a parliamentary commission on the December 1989 events. The ruling PDSR senatores say it was a revolution, while opposition representatives insist it was a coup.

- "Votes for poverty" reads a headline comparing living standards in the 42 counties with the percentage of votes recorded by each of the two presidential contenders. In the poorest counties, Iliescu led with 50 percent, Constantinescu trails with up to 20. In counties with a high living standard the figures were reversed.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- It would be a catastrophe for the country and for Iliescu himself if he stayed in office after Sunday's run-off, says an editorial. There is a historic need, both in local and international terms, for Iliescu to be in opposition.
- The newspaper publishes a document issued by the former Communist Party appointing Iliescu as full member of the party's Central committee in April 1968.
CRONICA ROMANA

- The PDSR executive president Adrian Nastase says that the new parliamentary majority built by the CDR and Petre Roman's Social Democratic Union (USD) will have to negociate with the PDSR to adopt important laws. ($=3,470 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
